title: Tenant-proportional reservation smoothing for reserved capacity burst protection
creator: Asha Kapoor
description:
Problem: Customers in Dedicated pools see bursty token consumption that occasionally exhausts per-tenant reserved windows even when pool-level capacity exists. Current implementations use per-tenant fixed buckets + rolling-window resets which leads to short-term unfairness and sudden throttles after timezone-aligned resets or delayed epoch reconciliation. This causes noisy throttles, customer support incidents, and billing reconciliation complexity.

Proposal: Implement a Tenant-Proportional Reservation Smoothing (TPRS) algorithm in the quota allocator. Key ideas: 1) Maintain a soft per-tenant reservation credit that is smoothed across a configurable time constant (alpha) rather than strict epoch-level top-ups. 2) When pool utilization is low, unused reservation credits are stochastically redistributed to active tenants (proportional to recent usage) as temporary burst buffers. 3) Enforce hard invariants: the sum of active credits may never exceed the pool commit; transient borrowing requires escrow accounting to ensure downstream billing correctness. 4) Provide deterministic fallback to the existing rolling-window reset for tenants opted-out or during incidents.

Why different from existing tickets: Rather than changing epoch boundaries or resetting logic, TPRS focuses on dynamic, proportional smoothing and temporary redistribution within reserved pools to reduce abrupt throttles and improve fairness. This addresses both timezone drift and intra-pool capacity waste.

Technical details:
- Data model: Per-tenant objects: allocated_commit, smoothed_credit (float), last_update_ts, recent_usage_ema (exp. decaying with window w=5m default).
- Smoothing step (run on allocator tick or per-request adjust): smoothed_credit := smoothed_credit * (1 - alpha) + (allocated_commit * alpha) - consumed_since_last. Alpha default 0.05 (configurable per pool).
- Redistribution: If pool_free_capacity > threshold and tenant_recent_usage_pct > min_activity, allow temporary_burst := min(pool_free_capacity * redistribution_ratio, allocated_commit * burst_cap_mult). Track as borrowed_credit with expiration and repayment schedule (linear over next N ticks).
- Billing correctness: All borrowed_credit events are logged to the usage ledger with borrow_epoch and repay_deadline. A reconciliation job guarantees any unrepaid borrow at monthly close is settled against pool-level credits and reflected in billing invoices.
- Invariants & safety: hard caps, per-tenant deny policy for excessive borrowing, global circuit-breaker (if pool_utilization > 95% disable redistribution).

Implementation plan:
1) Design & simulation (2 weeks): build simulator with historical production traces (last 30 days) to tune alpha, redistribution_ratio, burst_cap_mult.
2) Quota allocator changes (3 weeks): add smoothed_credit state, update per-request checks, add borrow ledger entry.
3) Telemetry & dashboards (1 week): new metrics: tenant_smoothed_credit, tenant_borrowed_credit, pool_reallocation_events, reconciliation_lag.
4) Backfill/reconciliation job (1 week): nightly job to detect unrepaid borrows, create accounting adjustments.
5) Gradual rollout (2+ weeks): canary on non-critical clusters, opt-in by tenant, monitor for regressions, automatic rollback toggle.

Rollout strategy: Start with internal test orgs -> 5 small beta tenants in us-west -> expand to low-risk Dedicated pools -> full rollout if SLOs maintain. During rollout, default to conservative parameters (alpha=0.02, redistribution_ratio=0.1).

Acceptance criteria:
- 30% reduction in abrupt per-tenant throttles during peak windows in simulation and canary tenants.
- No increase in invoice discrepancies beyond 0.1% margin caused by borrow settlements.
- End-to-end latency impact < 2ms per request for quota check path.

Observability and alerts:
- Alert if tenant_borrowed_credit > 30% of allocated_commit for > 1h.
- Alert if reconciliation_lag > 24h.
- Grafana panel for per-pool redistribution heatmap and per-tenant borrow timeline.

Migration and rollback:
- Provide 'smoothing_enabled' flag per-pool. Rollback by disabling flag and running immediate repay reconciliation to convert borrowed credits back to ledger-neutral state.

Trade-offs:
- Pros: fewer abrupt throttles, improved fairness, better utilization of reserved capacity.
- Cons: increases complexity of allocator state and billing reconciliation; small risk of billing confusion for customers without clear telemetry; must be conservative to avoid over-allocation.

2025-02-25 - Liam Chen (SRE): Concern: race between allocator ticks and high-concurrency bursts. Proposed per-request atomic borrow-check and fallback semaphore to avoid double-counting. Added circuit-breaker condition when pool_utilization > 95%.

2025-03-01 - Code review (PR #1234): Feedback from reviewers: split ledger write into async append + sync checkpoint to reduce latency; include idempotency tokens for borrow entries. Mateo addressed comments and pushed PR-1234 with changes.

2025-03-03 - UX review (Dave Lin, Design): Suggestion to show a 'burst credit' timeline in Console per-tenant and expose explainable message in throttling responses e.g., 'throttled - temporary-burst-exhausted'. Added to telemetry plan.
